extracted.intended_audience: community college administrators, faculty, and staff preparing grant/project proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and improving community college project/grant proposals to increase fundability. Focuses on meeting funder requirements, providing specific plans and evidence, cost-effectiveness, documentation of partners/personnel, and internal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet the Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Read carefully the restrictions and guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the proposal strictly follows the funder's stated criteria, restrictions, and submission guidelines before preparing and submitting the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present Specific Facts and Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: List specific classes, forums and seminars identified as to topic, cost and duration; include supporting material such as newspaper articles or any other evidence that the stated need of the community does indeed exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concrete: identify exact activities, their topics, costs, and lengths. Provide external evidence (e.g., newspaper clippings, data) to substantiate the community need the project addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Proposal Development a Year-Round Effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication with community and college personnel should be on a continuing basis in regard to needs; a 'proposal bank' should be maintained that reflects community needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain ongoing engagement with stakeholders to identify needs continually and keep a repository of proposal ideas ('proposal bank') so applications are developed proactively rather than hastily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose Economic Solutions to Problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't propose an activity that entails a high unit cost per participant if the same activity can be carried out at local colleges or universities for a lesser cost; be wary of the use of high-paid consultants in the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate cost-effectiveness: compare unit costs to local alternatives, justify expensive items or consultants, and avoid proposing unnecessarily costly approaches that funders can view as inefficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document the Involvement of Persons and Institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Include supporting material such as letters or resolutions from other institutions that might participate in the proposed work; if the proposed project depends upon key personnel, include resumes giving their qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach letters of support/commitment from partner organizations and CVs/resumes for key staff to substantiate capacity and collaborative commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triple Check Your Figures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully verify all numerical information (budgets, counts, calculations) for accuracy and internal consistency to avoid errors that undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check Out Proposal on Campus before Submitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your proposal to several persons for editing and reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have multiple campus reviewers edit and critique the proposal prior to submission to catch problems, improve clarity, and strengthen arguments.
